newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-HINGIS CRUSHES PIERCE TO REACH TOSHIBA CLASSIC FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS CRUSHES PIERCE TO REACH TOSHIBA CLASSIC FINAL.

text.p: World number one Martina Hingis stormed into her 10th final of the year Saturday with an overpowering semifinal victory over sixth seed Mary Pierce at the Toshiba Tennis Classic.
The 16-year-old Swiss sensation played a near flawless match and even unleashed seven aces for a 6-0 6-2 49-minute thumping of Pierce in a rematch of the Australian Open final.
"I played so good, I almost didn't make one error," Hingis said with a broad smile.

Hingis, who last Sunday added her eighth title of the year to her Australian Open and Wimbledon crowns, goes for number nine Sunday against either second seed Monica Seles or third seed Amanda Coetzer, who were to clash in a night semifinal.

The top seed, who ran her 1997 match record to 53-1 -- her lone blemish a defeat in the French Open final -- stroked 21 winners but was especially proud of her performance from the service line Saturday.
"For me, it was always hard to serve and return well in the same match, but that's what I did today. I was so happy with my serve."

Pierce had been in such good form in her quarter-final win over French compatriot Sandrine Testud Friday that it seemed she might be able to give Hingis a contest. But that challenge never materialised with Pierce winning just eight points in the brief first set.

"I don't know what to say," she laughed. "Today, I just didn't have it like in the other matches. I'm just really disappointed I didn't play well to give myself a chance and see what I can do against her."
Despite an edge in experience and three previous victories over Hingis, Pierce fell victim to self-imposed pressure and was never in the match.
"I was trying to make too good of a shot," she said. "I was going for it too soon instead of giving her a chance to make a mistake.
"This match to me wasn't a match," Pierce said.
"When you lose the first set 6-0 in 18 minutes, you know nothing happened. It was just mistake, next point."
But the next point wasn't much better for Pierce, who double-faulted away the opening game of the second set as the rout continued to its inevitable conclusion.
"Mary, she was trying but she played a very risky match," Hingis said, "and I played a great match."
